travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise normal precautionin Malaysia. Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory.
Malaysia is generally a safe destination for travelers.
Exercise increased caution on islands and maritime areas off the coast of Eastern Sabah from Kudat in the north to Tawau in the south due to risk of kidnapping.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Japanese Encephalitis vaccination is recommended if spending more than a month in rural areas or during mosquito season.

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 10am-10pm daily. Chain pharmacies like Guardian, Watsons, and CARING are widely available. Some 24-hour pharmacies in major cities. Rural areas have fewer pharmacies with shorter hours.
pharmacy.tips: Many common OTC medications are available. Some prescription medications in other countries are available OTC in Malaysia. Generic medications are widely available and affordable. Malaysian pharmacists often speak English. Prescription requirements are enforced for antibiotics and controlled substances.

water.notes: Tap water is generally safe to drink in major cities like Kuala Lumpur and Penang, though many locals prefer bottled water. Bottled water is widely available and inexpensive. In rural areas, drink bottled or purified water.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Malaysia is famous for its food — hawker centers and street food are generally safe and delicious. Malaysia has excellent food safety standards in restaurants. Be cautious with raw seafood and ensure meats are thoroughly cooked. Stick to busy, popular food stalls where turnover is high.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not required but strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Malaysia has excellent private hospitals at a fraction of Western prices. Medical care is affordable — a specialist consultation costs 80-150 MYR ($18-35 USD). Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is still recommended for emergencies. Malaysia's geographic position means evacuation to Singapore or Thailand may be needed for serious conditions.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Excellent quality healthcare, especially in Kuala Lumpur, Penang, and other major cities. Malaysia has a strong medical tourism industry — private hospitals in KL are internationally accredited (JCI) with world-class facilities and English-speaking staff. Public hospitals are adequate but may have longer waits. Dental care is also excellent and affordable.

medications.prescriptionRules: Prescriptions from foreign doctors are accepted but may need verification. Antibiotics and controlled substances require Malaysian prescriptions. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter as backup documentation. Malaysian pharmacies are reliable for common medication needs.

restrictedMeds.name: Diazepam (Valium) and benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires Malaysian prescription or special permission from the Ministry of Health. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Quantities for personal use are permitted with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Products with codeine require prescription. Some codeine preparations may be available OTC in small doses.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription. Bring your documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Malaysian Ministry of Health permission. Contact the Malaysian embassy before traveling with ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Malaysia — severe penalties including death for trafficking. CBD products with no THC may be legal but are in a gray area — avoid bringing them.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry the original prescription. Declare all medications at customs.
medications.generalAdvice: Malaysia has among the world's strictest drug laws — drug trafficking carries a mandatory death penalty. All medications must be declared at customs, carried in original containers, and supported by a doctor's letter. The National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency controls medication imports strictly.

controlledSubstances.note: Completely illegal. Possession of more than 200g carries a mandatory death sentence. Even small amounts result in severe imprisonment. CBD products are also illegal.
Strictly controlled. Possession above certain thresholds triggers presumption of trafficking (mandatory death penalty). Carry only personal supply with comprehensive documentation.
Controlled under the Dangerous Drugs Act. Carry a doctor's letter, original packaging, and limit to personal travel supply. Declare at customs.
Controlled substances. Allowed with valid prescription and doctor's documentation. Keep in original containers and declare at customs.
Illegal under the Poisons Act 1952 despite traditional use in some areas. Possession is a criminal offense.
Mandatory death penalty for trafficking. Malaysia enforces drug laws with extreme severity. Do not carry any illegal substances.

connectivity.simOptions: Hotlink (Maxis), Celcom, or Digi at KLIA or 7-Eleven. RM30-50 for tourist plans.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Good WiFi at malls, hotels, cafes. Spotty in Borneo jungle.

cultural.tipping: Not expected. Some upscale restaurants add 10% service charge.
cultural.dressCode: Modest at mosques (robes provided). Remove shoes at mosques and homes.
cultural.greetings: Light handshake then touch heart. Don't offer handshake to opposite gender unless initiated.
cultural.haggling: Expected at night markets. Not at malls or supermarkets.

safety.lgbtSafety: Malaysia criminalizes same-sex relations under both civil and Sharia law, with penalties including imprisonment and caning. LGBTQ+ travelers must exercise extreme discretion. There is no visible queer scene and public displays of affection between same-sex couples are unsafe.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Malaysia is relatively safe for solo female travelers, especially in tourist areas like Kuala Lumpur, Penang, and Langkawi. Dress modestly in Muslim-majority areas. Grab (ride-hailing) is reliable and safe. Be cautious in isolated areas and avoid walking alone at night in unfamiliar neighborhoods.
safety.notes: Malaysia is a generally safe and tourist-friendly country with excellent infrastructure. Petty crime like snatch theft (motorcycle bag-grabbing) is the main concern, especially in Kuala Lumpur and Johor Bahru. Violent crime against tourists is rare. Be aware of strong currents at east coast beaches during monsoon season (November–March).

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free. Very easy entry.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: March-October for west coast. November-February for east coast. KL hot year-round.

hospitals.name: Gleneagles Hospital Kuala Lumpur
hospitals.notes: Top private hospital in KL. International patient services, English-speaking staff throughout.

hospitals.name: Penang Adventist Hospital
hospitals.notes: Leading hospital in Penang with strong international patient services.

immediate: Monitor JPS (Department of Irrigation and Drainage) flood alerts
Do not cross flooded roads — depths are deceptive
Move to higher floors if building is flooding
Follow evacuation to nearest flood relief center (Pusat Pemindahan Sementara)
after: Boil or purify water after flooding
Avoid contact with floodwater — leptospirosis risk
Report flood damage to local authority (Jabatan Kerja Raya)

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 999)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (999) and ambulance (999) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the LEFT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
